activity.notes: Oxford Classical Dictionary identifies Fritigern as leader of the Gothic Tervingi who seized power around 376 during the Hunnic crisis, led the group into Roman territory, won at Adrianople in 378 and was still in power around 380. ATLAS therefore uses the historically specific Tervingi identity rather than projecting the later Visigoths political community backward into the 370s.

sources.title: Fritigern — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: Peter Heather identifies Fritigern as leader of the Gothic Tervingi, in power from about 376 through about 380, and victor at Hadrianople in 378.

sources.title: The Goths — Encyclopaedia Britannica 1911
sources.citation_text: The historical reference describes the 376 Danube crossing under Frithigern and the Gothic victory at Adrianople in 378.
